title: Blob2 (blobext-03) on mimid-server: destroy without blobHasReference, fixed-lifetime touch, no lookup/convert
description:
Bead mimid-1wgh.14.7: serving draft-ietf-jmap-blobext-03 (urn:ietf:params:jmap:blob2) over mimid-server's blob store with crate-jmap's jmap-blob-server (rev b85dfc85), mainly for Blob/set destroy. mimid-server's blobs are sealed attachments referenced only from MLS ciphertext it cannot read (decision mimid-1wgh.67).

Questions and readings:

1. Destroy and blobHasReference (§4: "The server MUST reject any blob that is still referenced by another object"). (a) never destroy, since a reference may exist in ciphertext; (b) destroy always: no object the server can see references a blob, so the MUST has nothing to apply to. Chosen (b): it is the point of the bead (a sender deletes an attachment early), and the same reasoning as mimid-1wgh.67. A sender that destroys an attachment breaks the messages still pointing at it; that is its choice. Another account's blob is notFound (backend rule: invisible = missing).

2. Update ("touch", §4: the server "can honour the requested expires ... or return a different expires value"). (a) reset the lifetime from now; (b) keep the fixed lifetime from creation and answer with the expires in force. Chosen (b): mimid-1wgh.67 is a fixed lifetime from upload, and assetLifetime promises recipients exactly that; extending it would need its own decision.

3. Which methods. blob2 names Blob/set, get, lookup, convert. Chosen: all four registered; lookup with supportedTypeNames [] (§2.1: "If the array is empty, the server does not support Blob/lookup", so every call is unknownDataType); convert with every conversion list null (every entry invalidProperties from the handler). RFC 9404 (urn:ietf:params:jmap:blob, Blob/upload) not advertised, Blob/upload not registered; RFC 8620 §6.3 Blob/copy not registered (a token reaches one account only).

4. Methods called without blob2 in using (§4-§8: each "requires that capability in the request's using array"; no error named). Chosen: unknownMethod (RFC 8620 §3.6.2), as the method is not one the request enabled. The handlers alone would run them in blobext mode.

5. Capability values (all INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC where a number): maxSizeBlobSet = BlobQuota.max_len (MAX_BLOB_LEN, as maxSizeUpload); maxDataSources 64 (the §2.1 minimum); supportedDigestAlgorithms ["sha-256"] (computed on read; §2.1 SHOULD list only efficient ones, none stored, sha-256 is the cheapest safe one); uploadUrl, chunkSize, conversion lists and limits null.

6. Create. Supported: sources concatenated, stored as an upload under the same quota (tooLarge / overQuota SetErrors), type hint stored as given, application/octet-stream when null. noPersist blobs are persisted like any other (§4: the server "is not required to persist it", so persisting is allowed). Blob/get imageData always null; chunks the one-chunk default.

For Mark to judge.
